stem: A grower increases irrigation frequency after seeing leaf droop, but the root zone was already persistently wet. What is the strongest critique?
choices: Leaf droop alone does not distinguish water deficit from poor root-zone aeration or other stress; root-zone conditions should be checked before increasing irrigation
Root-zone moisture cannot affect leaf appearance
Only nutrient strength should be evaluated
rationale: Similar shoot symptoms can arise from different root-zone conditions. Irrigation changes should be based on measured water status and root context, not one visual symptom.
